title.en: Explain schema, instance, constraint, meta-data, query, data manipulation and database engine

say.en: When you book a train ticket, millions of people are reading and changing the same seat data at the same time, yet two people never get the same berth. Software called a DBMS makes this possible. In this lesson: Define database and DBMS.
Explain schema, instance, constraint, meta-data, query, data manipulation and database engine.

body.en: A *database* is an organised collection of logically related data. A database management system (DBMS) is software to create, store, retrieve, update and manage databases. It reduces redundancy, keeps data consistent, controls who can see what, and lets users get answers through queries. Examples of DBMS: MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQLite, Microsoft Access. Real-life uses: banking, railway reservation, library, online shopping, hospitals.

points.en: DBMS examples: MySQL, Oracle, PostgreSQL, SQLite

title.en: On the board: Where the DBMS sits

say.en: Users and application programs never touch the stored files directly. They go through the DBMS.
The DBMS stores the database and a data dictionary: metadata, which is data about the data.
The schema is the design: tables, columns, types and constraints. An instance is the data at one moment.
A query asks the DBMS for data, and a constraint such as NOT NULL restricts what may be stored.

narration.en: We place the DBMS between users and the stored database, and separate the schema from the instance.

say.en: We place the DBMS between users and the stored database, and separate the schema from the instance.

explanation.en: The schema is the design and rarely changes; the instance is a snapshot that changes all the time. Constraints, meta-data, queries and the engine together let the DBMS keep data correct and answer questions.

body.en: *Database* schema: the design of the database (tables, attributes, types, constraints). Data constraint: a restriction on the values allowed, such as NOT NULL or UNIQUE. Meta-data / data dictionary: data about the database, stored by the DBMS. Database instance: the data stored at a particular moment. Query: a request to retrieve or change data. Data manipulation: insertion, deletion and updation. Database engine: the core component that creates and processes data.

narration.en: The schema is the design, the instance is the data at one moment, constraints restrict values, the data dictionary keeps meta-data, and the engine does the actual work.
narration.kn: ಸ್ಕೀಮಾ ವಿನ್ಯಾಸ, ಇನ್‌ಸ್ಟೆನ್ಸ್ ಒಂದು ಕ್ಷಣದ ದತ್ತಾಂಶ, ನಿರ್ಬಂಧಗಳು ಮೌಲ್ಯಗಳನ್ನು ನಿಯಂತ್ರಿಸುತ್ತವೆ, ದತ್ತಾಂಶ ನಿಘಂಟು ಮೆಟಾಡೇಟಾ ಇಡುತ್ತದೆ, ಎಂಜಿನ್ ನಿಜವಾದ ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: Let us work through this together. For a library database, classify each: i 'BOOK has columns AccNo, Title, Price', ii 'Price must be greater than 0', iii the 1,200 books stored today, iv 'List books costing more than 500 rupees'.
i Structure of the table gives schema.
ii Restriction on allowed values gives data constraint.
iii Data present at this moment gives database instance.
iv Request for data gives query.
So the answer is i schema, ii constraint, iii instance, iv query.
